assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a forcing, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general operation. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, chelating bisphosphines) made the transformation broad and predictable. It is among the most widely used reactions in medicinal and process chemistry, visible in countless syntheses and in industry, which is exactly the criterion of a method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds.
assessment.attribution: The decisive conceptual and practical development of general catalytic amination is conventionally associated with Buchwald and Hartwig. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor but a stoichiometric-tin method; whether it merits laureate status or a footnote is a judgment call. Two laureates give a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Roughly three decades of use, extensive independent confirmation and industrial scale adoption. The 2010 Nobel Prize for cross-coupling recognized Pd coupling broadly but not C-N coupling specifically, so recognition is now overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Weight of Kosugi's and Migita-type precedent; I recall but have not verified the detailed priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened single-electron pathways under mild conditions with simple light sources, enabling new bond disconnections and late-stage functionalization, and it combines with other catalytic modes (dual catalysis, Ni cross-coupling). The change in synthetic logic is real and broadly adopted in academia and pharmaceutical discovery.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 reports of Yoon, MacMillan and Stephenson are generally regarded as the modern founding works. Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre have strong claims, and the field has many contributors. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which complicates a second recognition for him. A fair three-person set is possible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Field is about 15 years old, widely replicated, and industrially used in flow and medicinal chemistry; the mechanistic picture is still evolving. Recognition is plausible but could be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: MacMillan's prior Nobel recognition may weigh against him.
Large number of credible contributors makes the credit allocation unstable.
Some reported transformations may be rebranded known photochemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ligand- and directing-group-controlled catalytic C-H functionalization converts ubiquitous C-H bonds into synthetic handles with site- and enantioselectivity, shortening routes to complex molecules and fitting the efficiency theme of modern synthesis. Yu's ligand-accelerated and template strategies and Sanford's Pd/high-valent chemistry are conceptual advances, not only scope extensions.
assessment.attribution: Yu is the most prominent for general ligand-enabled Pd C-H activation, with Sanford (Pd(II)/Pd(IV) and fluorination) and Hartwig (borylation) as strong complements. Daugulis and Smith also have clear priority claims (directing groups, borylation), so the three-name limit forces hard exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of development, with growing late-stage and process use, though truly general predictable selectivity remains incomplete. Maturity is reasonable but less settled than cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Hartwig's overlap with B035 may be an issue if both are awarded.
Industrial uptake is still narrower than for cross-coupling.
Disputed boundaries between sub-areas (directing groups, borylation, oxidative functionalization).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide segments at cysteine, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical. It is a clearly new, general chemical reaction with large downstream impact in protein science and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Kent and colleagues (1994) introduced NCL; Muir developed expressed protein ligation, which extended it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky and others contributed extensions (desulfurization, glycoprotein synthesis). Kent, Dawson and Muir form a defensible trio, with some credit ambiguity around the original paper's co-authors.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use, many independent applications, mature. The Merrifield (1984) and Sanger-type protein-chemistry recognitions precede it; timely or arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Co-author credit on the original 1994 report is unresolved.
Border with biology; chemical novelty is clear, but committee appetite is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes showed that these formerly transient species could be bottled, then developed into ubiquitous ligands (NHCs) and organocatalysts. Their effect on catalysis, including olefin metathesis catalysts, and main-group chemistry is large and conceptually simple.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand (stable phosphinocarbene, 1988) and Arduengo (crystalline NHC, 1991) are the foundational names; Nolan's contribution is mainly NHC-metal catalysis development, which is important but more of an application. Bode and Rovis are NHC organocatalysis rather than the isolation itself.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years, very well confirmed and broadly applied. Timeliness is good; the metathesis context overlaps with the 2005 prize, which partly weakens uniqueness.
uncertainties: Some of the impact is already credited through metathesis (2005 prize).
Whether Nolan or an organocatalysis name should be included instead of a third laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry is the enabling chemistry for automated oligonucleotide synthesis and underpins PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a case of synthetic method design with enormous downstream influence, and its efficiency (near-quantitative coupling cycles) is what made the technology routine.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers is the clear originator of the phosphoramidite method (1981). Hood is credited for automation instrumentation, which is less a chemical discovery; I would not include him. Beaucage's contribution is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, over 40 years of near-universal use. Recognition has long been possible, which raises doubt about why it hasn't occurred, but it is entirely timely on merit.
uncertainties: The role of Beaucage and others is outside the supplied credited names.
Possible committee view that it is enabling technology more than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs show that sterically hindered acid-base combinations can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, opening metal-free hydrogenation and a new bonding paradigm. It is conceptually simple and chemically new.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 report of reversible H2 activation and Erker's related work are the two obvious names, giving a clean two-laureate configuration; Welch and others are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen to twenty years old, independently confirmed, but practical impact in catalysis and industry remains modest compared with transition metal methods. Possibly premature.
uncertainties: Mechanistic debates over some FLP reactivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors fuse engineered deaminases to a Cas protein to make programmable single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks, a new chemical-biology tool with direct therapeutic relevance. The chemical novelty is protein-engineering and nucleoside deamination design rather than a new bond-forming reaction.
assessment.attribution: Liu, with Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor), is a natural trio; Nishida and Kondo's independent cytidine deaminase work complicates priority. Liu's CRISPR-adjacent profile also overlaps with B016 and B055.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation and rapid clinical translation within about a decade; very high impact but the field is still young, and the CRISPR prize (2020) already covers genome editing.
uncertainties: Border-field issue: what is new chemically versus biologically.
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with other Liu candidacies.
Independent contribution of Nishida and Kondo.
